assessments.reasoning: GNU’s lgpl-2.1.txt bears the FSF copyright and the exact dated heading. The two contiguous captures cover all 26,419 bytes and report the scoped SHA-256. Section 0 identifies the authorized notice that connects this text to a particular work.

The public-data-admission-taxonomy capture resolves to the License row of the Index’s SCOPE.md at cdff8aeed68bf1f9c62d8c86159c7dc08b2d75d7, bytes [533,639). Its requirements for a grant, identifiable text and identifiable edition are each met by the FSF publication.

challenge.method: Under pinned SCES-1.0 §§3–4 and Protocol stage 7, I tested two possible identity errors against the title, introductory edition note and §§0, 1, 6 and 13: merging this edition with GNU Library Public License version 2 and classifying the whole instrument as a linking exception.
challenge.results: The edition note calls Library version 2 its predecessor and identifies 2.1 as the first released Lesser GPL. Section 1 grants copying and distribution rights directly. Section 6 provides an exception within this numbered license. Neither the lineage nor that internal provision displaces the edition’s license identity.

limitations: A particular project’s notice must establish its grant, version choice and any modifications. The sample notice at the end illustrates how a publisher can apply the terms.
reasoning: The FSF text identifies the GNU Lesser General Public License by its heading “Version 2.1, February 1999” and supplies the operative grants in that edition. Together these satisfy the Index criterion for a license with identifiable text and edition. “Active” is the proposed Index lifecycle for that edition.
